name: How a new idea spreads
idea: An encyclopedia entry states that the work's theory treats diffusion as the spread of an innovation, passed on through channels over time, among members of a social system. It states that potential adopters judge an innovation by five characteristics, such as its advantage over alternatives and its fit with existing values and tools. Adopters, it states, fall into five groups.
suggests: Look at who has already taken up a new product or practice in a market, and at whether its advantage and its fit with what buyers already use help or slow its spread to the next group.
limits: The entry states that the diffusion model cannot predict how long adoption will take or what level it will reach. It also states that the author sorts criticisms of diffusion research into four groups, among them a pro-innovation bias that implies every innovation should be adopted.
competing_idea: The entry states that other researchers propose modelling diffusion with parametric formulas, as a means to forecast when adoption happens and how far it goes.
questions: Which groups of adopters have taken up this innovation so far, and which have yet to adopt it?
How do potential adopters judge its advantage over alternatives and its fit with what they use now?
Through which channels and networks does word of it travel among potential adopters?

originals.reference: Wikipedia contributors, "Diffusion of innovations", Wikipedia, The Free Encyclopedia, revision 1384697309 of 9 November 2026
originals.about: Everett M. Rogers, Diffusion of Innovations, Free Press of Glencoe, 1962, 367 pages
